what_changed: NCUA proposes removing 12 CFR 701.21(h) (third-party servicing of indirect vehicle loans: a federal credit union may purchase indirect vehicle loans and participations serviced by any one third-party servicer only up to 50 percent of net worth, rising to 100 percent after 30 months with that servicer, with a waiver process in (h)(2)-(3)), removing 741.203(c) (applying the same limits to federally insured state-chartered credit unions) and conforming 746.201(c). Credit union boards would set their own policies; NCUA would continue to review these purchases in examinations. Comments due May 26, 2026.
compliant_agent_must_now: No change until final (finalized without change by 2026-16029, effective September 8, 2026). If adopted, credit unions would no longer be capped on how much indirect auto paper serviced by a single third-party servicer (which could include a servicing provider using an AI agent) they may buy; oversight would rest on board policy, vendor due diligence and examination.
open_questions_for_deploying_team: Register gap: no row covers NCUA oversight of third-party servicers of indirect vehicle loans (former 12 CFR 701.21(h) and 741.203(c)). Should a VENDOR.GOVERNANCE row record the removal and the principles-based expectations that replace it?
Do credit union clients buy indirect vehicle loans serviced by the deployment's operator, and do their contracts or policies still reference the 701.21(h) limits?
rationale: Full text confirms the rule governs credit unions' exposure to third-party servicers of consumer auto loans, which touches how a servicing vendor is overseen. Confidence 0.7 because the rule is a concentration limit on loan purchases rather than a servicing-conduct or vendor-examination standard.
